Serendipity

/sair-uhn-DIP-ih-tee/ - the stress falls on DIP · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Serendipity means a fortunate discovery made by accident.

Half the apps on your phone began, their founders admit, in serendipity - a bug, a wrong file, a demo that failed in an interesting way.

Worked Example

Looking for her dropped earring under the theater seats, Amaya's flashlight caught a corner of paper taped beneath row F: a signed playbill from the opening night of 1962, exactly what the anniversary exhibit lacked. The earring stayed lost; the museum called it serendipity.

Serendipity is not plain luck: luck merely favors you, and coincidence merely happens. Serendipity requires a find - something valuable you were not looking for, delivered by accident to someone alert enough to notice it. Lose an earring, find an archive.

How Serendipity Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

luck

luck: good fortune of any kind, no discovery required

happenstance

happenstance: a neutral chance occurrence, lucky or not

windfall

windfall: an unexpected gain, usually money, found by no search at all

Antonyms

design

design: an outcome produced on purpose, by plan

misfortune

misfortune: chance working against you

How Strong Is It? — coincidence → luck → serendipity

coincidence vs. serendipity

coincidence vs. serendipity: Coincidence is two things merely happening together, with nothing gained; serendipity hands you a discovery.

luck vs. serendipity

luck vs. serendipity: Luck favors you in general - a green light, a good seat; serendipity is more particular, an accident that delivers a delightful find.

Sort It Out

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — serendip-

Root — serendip-: Serendip, an old name for Sri Lanka

Suffix — -ity

Suffix — -ity: state of being

Put it together

Put it together: Serendip- (Serendip, an old Persian name for the island of Sri Lanka) + -ity (the state of being) = 'Serendip-ness.' The writer Horace Walpole built the word in 1754, borrowing the fairy tale 'The Three Princes of Serendip,' whose heroes were always making discoveries, by accident, of things they were not seeking. The suffix is the genuine article; the base is a place on the map - proof that -ity was alive enough for an author to coin a brand-new word with it.

The fairy tale inside the word

The fairy tale inside the word: There is no root to reuse - Serendip is simply the old name for Sri Lanka. Horace Walpole invented serendipity in 1754 after the tale of the island's three princes, forever finding treasures they were not seeking. Every later use of the word retells their story in miniature.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral / warm

Serendipity is friendly and story-shaped; science writing and travel essays love it. Use luck for general good fortune; save serendipity for the moment an accident hands you a discovery - the word itself implies that something was found.
